primary_task: Build a tiered buyer universe (strategic buyers and financial sponsors) for a sell-side target and deliver it as an Excel workbook plus a one-page summary.

requirements.name: Excel workbook writer (e.g. openpyxl)
requirements.evidence: ### Step 6: Output - Excel workbook with: - Strategic buyers tab (sorted by tier) - Financial sponsors tab (sorted by tier) - Contact mapping for Tier 1 - Summary statistics
requirements.basis: tools.bash: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, ...)"; software: "installable"

requirements.name: company / M&A research (web_search or Bigdata.com connector)
requirements.evidence: Research recent M&A activity — buyers who just did a deal in the space are either hungry for more or tapped out ... Financial sponsors: check fund vintage and deployment pace
requirements.basis: tools.web_search: "search the public web and read result snippets"; tools.bigdata_com: "Bigdata.com connector (financial data and documents): bigdata_company_tearsheet, bigdata_search, find_securities, bigdata_fetch_document"

requirements.name: ask_user (target details, seller preferences)
requirements.evidence: Always ask the seller if there are buyers they want included or excluded
requirements.basis: tools.ask_user: "ask the user a question (with options) and read the answer in the conversation"

requirements.name: send_user_file
requirements.basis: tools.send_user_file: "send a file from the session to the user"

notes: Microsoft Excel itself is not needed; an .xlsx file can be written with a PyPI library. Research is one requirement satisfied by web_search or Bigdata.com; no paid M&A database (PitchBook, Capital IQ) is named. Direct fetches of company sites outside the allow-list are refused, which only limits depth.
